I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father did the same, and his father before him. At 65, I know this land well — the soil here on the North China Plain is good for wheat and maize. That's what I grow. That's what everyone around me grows. The government extension station promotes it, the seed shops stock for it, and my neighbors all do the same rotation. There's no reason to change.

I have about 10 mu of contracted land. I'll grow winter wheat on all of it — I sowed last October and it's coming up now — and then after the June harvest I'll plant summer maize on the same land and harvest that in September. Two crops a year, same as always.

For wheat, I'll irrigate four times. Water is expensive and the well is deep, but I can't risk a bad harvest. I'll put down the full fertilizer — I buy the compound fertilizer bag at the village co-op and add urea on top at jointing. That's what my neighbor Old Wang does and he gets good yields. For maize, the summer rains help, so maybe just two irrigations.

I use the rotary tiller my son helped me buy five years ago. Ploughing by hand is too hard at my age. I'll spray herbicide after sowing and fungicide before heading for the wheat. Maize gets herbicide and one more spray if I see corn borers.

I use the Jimai improved variety for wheat and Zhengdan 958 for maize — the seed shop has sold these for years, I trust them.
